items.stem: Name the hormone secreted by the pituitary gland and state one effect of its deficiency or excess.
items.answer: Growth hormone; deficiency causes dwarfism; excess causes gigantism.
items.markingKey: 1 mark hormone. 1 mark effect.

items.stem: Arrange these steps of a reflex arc (touching a hot object) in the correct order: (1) the receptor in the skin detects heat; (2) the sensory neuron carries the impulse; (3) the motor neuron carries the impulse; (4) the effector muscle contracts and the hand is pulled away; (5) the relay neuron in the spinal cord passes it on.
items.markingKey: Correct order: the receptor in the skin detects heat → the sensory neuron carries the impulse → the relay neuron in the spinal cord passes it on → the motor neuron carries the impulse → the effector muscle contracts and the hand is pulled away.

items.stem: Which of these is an example of phototropism?
items.answer: sunflower heads following the Sun
items.markingKey: (a) Sunflower heads following the Sun is an example of phototropism. The others: the pollen tube growing towards the ovule – an example of chemotropism; the shoot growing upwards away from gravity – an example of negative geotropism; roots growing towards a leaking pipe – an example of hydrotropism.
options: roots growing towards a leaking pipe
the pollen tube growing towards the ovule
the shoot growing upwards away from gravity

items.stem: Classify these as a voluntary action or a reflex action: writing a letter, riding a bicycle, sneezing.
items.answer: A voluntary action: riding a bicycle, writing a letter. A reflex action: sneezing.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): A voluntary action: riding a bicycle, writing a letter. A reflex action: sneezing.

items.stem: Why does a plant kept near a window bend towards it?
items.answer: Auxin collects on the shaded side of the shoot, making those cells grow longer, so the shoot bends towards light.
items.markingKey: 1 mark auxin shady side. 1 mark bending.

items.stem: Which hormone is secreted by the pancreas?
items.answer: insulin
items.markingKey: (c) Insulin is secreted by the pancreas. The others: growth hormone – secreted by the pituitary gland; thyroxin – secreted by the thyroid gland; testosterone – secreted by the testes.

items.stem: Classify these responses as an example of chemotropism or an example of phototropism: (1) sunflower heads following the Sun; (2) the pollen tube growing towards the ovule; (3) a shoot bending towards a window.
items.answer: An example of chemotropism: the pollen tube growing towards the ovule. An example of phototropism: a shoot bending towards a window; sunflower heads following the Sun.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): An example of chemotropism: the pollen tube growing towards the ovule. An example of phototropism: a shoot bending towards a window; sunflower heads following the Sun.

items.stem: Insulin is secreted by the:
items.answer: pancreas

items.stem: What are the limitations of using electrical impulses for coordination?
items.answer: They reach only cells connected by nerves, and a cell needs time to reset before sending a new impulse; they cannot act continuously.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem: Which of these is NOT a voluntary action?
items.answer: knee-jerk response
items.markingKey: (a) Knee-jerk response is a reflex action, not a voluntary action. Each of the others (walking to school, talking to a friend, riding a bicycle) is a voluntary action.

items.stem: Define thigmonasty.
items.answer: A non-directional movement in response to touch, as in the leaves of the touch-me-not plant
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Thigmonasty – a non-directional movement in response to touch, as in the leaves of the touch-me-not plant.
